title: Exponential Time Hypothesis
formal: Is \(s_3>0\) in the deterministic bit model defined below? Equivalently, does there exist one real \(c>0\) such that no 3-SAT decider A has a runtime bound \(t_A(F)\le C\,2^{c n(F)}(L(F)+1)^d\) on every valid 3-CNF formula F for any fixed integers \(C\ge1,d\ge0\)? The same positive c must exclude all such algorithms. This is the deterministic Exponential Time Hypothesis.
definitions: Fix an integer clause-width bound \(q\ge 3\). A q-CNF formula is a finite list of clauses, each a finite list of at most q literals. A literal is a variable \(x_i\) or its negation \(\neg x_i\), with \(1\le i\le n\). The variables that occur are exactly \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), so n counts distinct variables, not clauses or input bits. Repeated literals, repeated clauses and clauses containing both signs of a variable are allowed. A Boolean assignment satisfies the formula if every clause has at least one true literal. An empty clause is false; the empty conjunction is true and has n=0. For a completely specified binary encoding, let \(\operatorname{code}(a)\), for a nonnegative integer a, be \(1^b0\) followed by the b-bit binary expansion of a+1, where \(b=\lfloor\log_2(a+1)\rfloor+1\). Encode n and the number m of clauses with this code, then each clause by its coded length followed by its literals. Each literal is a sign bit (0 for positive, 1 for negated) and the code of its variable index. All indicated lists must be fully present, with no trailing bits, valid indices and every declared variable occurring. Let L be the complete bit length. Ill-formed strings, including clauses wider than q, are rejected. No density, satisfiability-count, occurrence or input-distribution promise is imposed. A q-SAT decider A is one uniform deterministic multitape Turing machine with a finite program and fixed finite tape alphabets, a read-only input tape and initially blank work tapes. Each transition reads or writes only the cells at the heads and moves each head by at most one cell. The total transition count includes parsing, input access and all internal work. A must halt on all inputs, decide satisfiability exactly on valid q-CNF formulas, and reject malformed strings in polynomial time in their length. It receives no advice, random bits, quantum operations, oracle or precomputed instance information. The machine may depend on the fixed q. For a valid formula F, let \(t_A(F)\) be its runtime and \(n(F),L(F)\) its variable count and bit length. An exponent \(\alpha\ge 0\) is attainable at width q if there exist such a decider A and fixed integers \(C\ge1,d\ge0\) with \(t_A(F)\le C\,2^{\alpha n(F)}(L(F)+1)^d\) for every valid q-CNF formula F. The constants are independent of F. Define \(s_q\) as the infimum of all attainable exponents. This set is nonempty because exhaustive assignment testing gives an attainable exponent 1, so \(0\le s_q\le1\). The infimum need not itself be attainable. Polynomial factors in L remain explicit, including when clauses are repeated many times. The chosen explicit syntax and malformed-input normalization do not impose a new satisfiability promise; they fix the bit model for the source’s exponential-rate question. This card specializes q to 3. Its negation, \(s_3=0\), means that for every real \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a 3-SAT decider \(A_\varepsilon\) with fixed constants \(C_\varepsilon,d_\varepsilon\) satisfying \(t_{A_\varepsilon}(F)\le C_\varepsilon 2^{\varepsilon n(F)}(L(F)+1)^{d_\varepsilon}\) on every valid formula. The machine and constants may depend on epsilon. This statement does not require one machine with a single subexponential runtime bound, nor a computable map from epsilon to a machine.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of \(s_3>0\) or of \(s_3=0\) for the explicitly defined rate. A positive answer requires a positive constant excluding every valid deterministic decider at that exponential rate, with any polynomial input factor. A negative answer must establish arbitrarily small attainable positive exponents with the stated quantifiers. A fixed improved positive exponent, a bound for a restricted algorithm class, or a conditional lower bound does not settle this question. No numerical estimate of \(s_3\) is requested: the target is its strict positivity.
why: ETH is the central hypothesis for ruling out subexponential exact algorithms and many fixed-parameter speedups. It turns the qualitative P versus NP question into a quantitative claim that can be transferred through carefully sized reductions.

importance.reason: A foundational quantitative hardness hypothesis underlying exact, parameterized, graph, and geometric algorithm lower bounds.

progress.text: Impagliazzo and Paturi define the exponential rates of bounded-width satisfiability and relate positive rate at width three to positive rates at other fixed widths. These are structural results about the hypothesis, not a proof of it.
The authors’ IPEC survey explicitly defines ETH by a positive infimum and distinguishes the number of variables from the complete input length.

The parameterized-algorithms textbook retains the positive-infimum definition, explains its distinction from ruling out a single subexponential algorithm, and gives consequences for parameterized complexity.

Liu gives a deterministic \(1.32793^n\) upper bound for 3-SAT up to polynomial factors, recorded in the checked March 2020 revision of the ICALP 2018 work. This leaves the positivity of the optimal rate unresolved.

Aggarwal, Gupta, Morolia and Zhang derive new lattice approximation hardness under ETH or randomized ETH, with different assumptions for their closest-vector and shortest-vector results. The paper still treats these as assumptions and distinguishes Gap-ETH.

status_note: The original sources and the July 2026 ICALP paper continue to use ETH as an unproved hypothesis. The optimal-rate definition and cited algorithmic upper bound were checked against the full relevant source passages. Targeted later-work searches on 14 September 2026 found no verified resolution; bounded searches do not independently verify the cited proofs or exhaust all later literature.

context_blocks.text: NP-completeness describes the possibility of polynomial-time algorithms and does not itself impose a positive exponential rate. Even if P differs from NP, a running time such as \(2^{\sqrt{n}}\) remains possible for 3-SAT. ETH asks for a stronger obstruction: some fixed amount of exponential work must remain unavoidable when complexity is measured by the number of Boolean choices.

That parameter must be preserved carefully by a reduction. An ordinary polynomial-time reduction may turn an n-variable formula into an instance of size \(n^{3}\), which can destroy a claimed exponential lower bound in the new parameter. Sparsification supplies a controlled disjunction of bounded-density formulas, allowing variables and clauses to be related without an arbitrary polynomial blowup. This is a main reason ETH can support sharp bounds across many problems.

The infimum over all algorithms matters. Excluding one \(2^{o(n)}\) algorithm is the common informal wording, but the textbook explicitly keeps the stronger positive-infimum statement because the converse is unclear. ETH would be false if arbitrarily small constant exponents were attainable, even if the known algorithms depended on the desired exponent. A card that omitted this distinction would change the quantified question.

Liu’s deterministic algorithm has runtime \(O(1.32793^n)\) up to polynomial input factors. It therefore supplies an upper bound on \(s_3\); it establishes neither a positive lower bound nor the value of \(s_3\). The existence of one algorithm with a positive exponential rate does not rule out a much faster algorithm. Empirical solver success and promises on the formula are also distinct from this all-input infimum.

ETH is weaker than SETH, whose optimal rates approach one as the fixed clause width grows. It also differs from randomized ETH and from Gap-ETH, which asks for hardness of distinguishing fully satisfiable formulas from formulas with a constant unsatisfied fraction. Recent lattice reductions illustrate the value of tracking these distinctions: some approximation hardness can be obtained from deterministic ETH, while other results use randomized ETH. They extend the consequences of assumptions without proving the assumptions.

A single fixed exponent in ETH must obstruct every algorithm. Refuting one proposed lower-bound constant does not suffice, because another smaller positive constant could still work. Conversely, a refutation may use a different finite algorithm for each desired exponent; no effective procedure generating those algorithms is added to the target.

sentences: ETH asks whether the optimal deterministic exponential rate for 3-SAT is strictly positive.
The exponential parameter is the number of distinct variables, while polynomial factors account for the complete encoded input.
One positive rate must obstruct every algorithm, and refutation permits different algorithms for arbitrarily small positive rates.
Known exponential-time algorithms provide upper bounds but no positive lower bound on the optimum.
The hypothesis supports quantitative lower bounds throughout exact and parameterized algorithms without being established by those conditional consequences.
